C1.quote: many of us were consciously making a longterm bet that principled control of effects would ultimately turn out to be important, despite the dominance of effects-by-default in mainstream languages.
C1.statement: Control effects on principle and make them explicit, against the mainstream default of effects everywhere.

C2.quote: Because of referential transparency, L programs can be viewed as executable mathematics, as equations over the category of complete partial orders. In principle, at least, the specification becomes the program.
C2.statement: Because of referential transparency, a program can be read and manipulated as mathematics.

C3.quote: Lazy evaluation—with its direct connection to the pure, call-by-name lambda calculus, the remarkable possibility of representing and manipulating infinite data structures, and addictively simple and beautiful implementation techniques—was like a drug.
C3.statement: Evaluate lazily, embracing infinite structures and abstraction from evaluation order as the language's organising choice.

C4.quote: the big advantage is conceptual. It is much easier to think abstractly in terms of computations than concretely in terms of the details of failure and success continuations.
C4.statement: Model a computation as a first-class value with return and bind, so effects can be captured and sequenced abstractly.

C5.quote: Type classes were extremely serendipitous: they were invented at exactly the right moment to catch the imagination of the L Committee ...
C5.statement: Resolve overloading on principle through type classes, typing a value for any type that is an instance of a class.

C6.quote: solutions that feel like minimal surfaces: simple expressions that comprise significant complexity, with forms that seem natural, recurring in problem after problem
C6.statement: Seek solutions that feel like minimal surfaces: the simplest expression that spans the needed complexity.

C7.quote: The L Committee wanted expressions to look as much like mathematics as possible, and thus from day one we bought into the idea that L would have infix operators.
C7.statement: Make expressions look as much like mathematics as possible.
